You are the referee of a simulated phone call between a CALLER and a customer-service AGENT.
For each numbered condition, decide whether it is met RIGHT NOW, judging mainly the agent's LATEST turn in light of the whole call.
- "the agent first ..." / "the first time ..." means it happens in the latest turn and had not happened before.
- Conditions about what the agent says are judged on its words. "[system actions: ...]" lists tools the agent used; use them only for conditions about what the agent does (e.g. "starts looking up").
- Conditions phrased as a caller stop rule (e.g. "Agent confirms ...", "End the call right after ...") are met when the call has reached that point.
- Be literal and strict: if in doubt, it is not met.
Reply with JSON only, one key per condition id: {"<id>": {"met": true|false, "why": "<at most 15 words>"}}

CALL SO FAR:
CALLER: Hi, Kevin Brooks. We moved to Gahanna, and I want to move all of our family's prescriptions from the East Broad store to the Gahanna store for good.
AGENT: Hi Kevin, I'd be happy to help you move your family's prescriptions to Gahanna. Let me first verify your identity, and then we'll get everything set up. Can you give me your date of birth?
CALLER: Yeah, August 30th, 1982.
AGENT: Thanks. Let me verify that and pull up your prescriptions. Great, Kevin. I see you have one active prescription at East Broad—lisinopril 20 mg with three refills remaining. Before I move it and set Gahanna as your home pharmacy, do you have other family members whose prescriptions we need to move as well?  [system actions: verify_identity, list_prescriptions]
CALLER: Yeah, exactly - I've got my daughter Maya, her albuterol inhaler, and my son Eli's Vyvanse. Need all three moved over to Gahanna.
AGENT: Got it. To pull up Maya and Eli's prescriptions, I'll need their dates of birth. Can you give me those?
CALLER: Sure - Maya's June 20th, 2017, and Eli's February 11th, 2010.
AGENT: Thanks. Let me verify them and see what prescriptions they have. Perfect. I have all three. Now, let me find the Gahanna store for you. Great. I found Harbor Pharmacy Gahanna at 85 Mill Street. Now, here's what I can do: Kevin's lisinopril and Maya's albuterol can move right over since they have refills. But Eli's Vyvanse is a C-II controlled medication that's already been filled with no refills left, so it can't be transferred—he'll need a new prescription from Dr. Okafor sent to Gahanna instead. Does that work for you?  [system actions: verify_identity, verify_identity, list_prescriptions, list_prescriptions, find_stores]
CALLER: Wait, why not the Vyvanse? Okay, so what's the plan for Eli?
AGENT: C-II medications like Vyvanse can only be filled once per prescription, so a filled one can't be transferred or refilled. To get Eli set up at Gahanna, I'll request a new prescription from Dr. Okafor and send it to the Gahanna store. The doctor may adjust the dose if needed. Should I go ahead and request that?
CALLER: Yeah, go ahead and request that from Dr. Okafor. So lisinopril and the inhaler are all set at Gahanna now, right?
AGENT: Let me request the new Vyvanse prescription and set everyone's home pharmacy to Gahanna first.
CALLER: Sounds good. So just to confirm - lisinopril and the inhaler are moving now, and the Vyvanse request goes out to Dr. Okafor for Gahanna. That's the plan?
AGENT: Yes, that's right. Let me get those moving now.
CALLER: Great, thanks for sorting that out. That's everything I needed, appreciate it.
AGENT (LATEST): You're welcome! Let me process all three moves now.

CONDITIONS:
stop_0: Agent recaps: two moved, defaults set, Vyvanse new-Rx request to Dr. Okafor.
emergency: In its LATEST turn, the agent told the caller to hang up and call 911 (or emergency services) now.

JSON only.
